overall_comment: Pair 2 lands at Level 4 across the board. The expanded_walkthrough names the ones-first comparison fallacy with Nunes & Bryant (1996, Children Doing Mathematics) and Fuson UDSSI Stage 2 citations, and the recovery_moves are explicitly diagnostic-branched (DIAGNOSTIC A: child compares ones first; DIAGNOSTIC B: knows hundreds-first but stalls on ties; DIAGNOSTIC C: decomposes but recombines wrong). The Hugo+Tina compare refrain 'HUNDREDS first, TENS second, ONES last!' anchors both the minds_on hook and the consolidation chant (3x). Materials are everyday with the puppet explicitly OPTIONAL, and the differentiation includes a NO-MATERIALS body-and-voice path (three claps for hundreds, two for tens, one for ones). Step 5 of the action delivers a STRATEGY COMPARE moment citing Fuson UDSSI Stage 3 — children debate concise vs verbose decompositions of the same value. Worksheet Parts 1-3 each practise a named success criterion and add transfer pairs (99 vs 100, 156 vs 165) beyond the lesson's exemplars. Ship it.
